understanding: The task requires modifying TelegramReporter.report() in src/oko/live/reporters.py to check if bridge_output.incident_video_path exists and points to a valid file. If so, send the video via Telegram sendVideo API using multipart/form-data with the MP4 file in the 'video' field and bridge_output.description as the caption. Otherwise, fall back to the existing sendPhoto(keyframe) mechanism. Implementation must be minimal, committed directly, and all tests must pass.
summary: Add conditional logic in TelegramReporter.report() to prioritize sendVideo when incident_video_path is present and the file exists, using description as caption; otherwise preserve existing sendPhoto fallback.

decision_atoms.statement: Check bridge_output.incident_video_path existence and file validity before choosing sendVideo vs sendPhoto
decision_atoms.reason: The task explicitly requires sendVideo only when the path is set and the file exists; otherwise fallback to sendPhoto. This single concern keeps the change minimal.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds one conditional branch and file-existence check, slightly increasing method complexity but fully backward-compatible.

decision_atoms.statement: Use bridge_output.description as the caption parameter in sendVideo
decision_atoms.reason: Task specifies caption=bridge_output.description (VLM-generated text). This provides context for the video incident.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: If description is empty/None, Telegram will simply receive no caption, which is acceptable and matches the spec's intent.

decision_atoms.statement: Keep existing sendPhoto(keyframe) call unchanged as the else branch
decision_atoms.reason: Preserves backward compatibility for all cases without video, ensuring zero regression on existing functionality.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: None — pure additive change with fallback preservation.

decision_atoms.statement: Implement sendVideo using multipart/form-data with the MP4 file in the 'video' field
decision_atoms.reason: Telegram Bot API requires multipart/form-data for file uploads; the 'video' field name is the API parameter for sendVideo.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Requires proper file handling (opening in binary mode) and correct MIME type, but this is standard for Telegram API integration.

assumptions: bridge_output is an object with attributes incident_video_path (str or None) and description (str or None)
The existing TelegramReporter class has access to a Telegram client/bot instance capable of sendVideo and sendPhoto
The MP4 file at incident_video_path is a valid video file readable by the process
The existing sendPhoto method signature and behavior remain unchanged
Tests will mock HTTP calls to Telegram API to verify correct endpoint selection

risks.risk: Large video files may cause timeout or memory issues during upload
risks.mitigation: Consider adding file size validation or streaming upload in a future iteration; for now, rely on Telegram's 50MB limit and ensure reasonable video lengths from VLM pipeline

risks.risk: Race condition if incident_video_path file is deleted between existence check and sendVideo call
risks.mitigation: Wrap sendVideo in try/except for FileNotFoundError and fall back to sendPhoto in that edge case

risks.risk: bridge_output.description may contain characters that break Telegram caption formatting
risks.mitigation: Telegram API handles standard UTF-8 text; no special escaping needed unless markdown mode is used, which is not specified here

minimal_version: Add os.path.isfile check for incident_video_path; if True, call sendVideo with open(path,'rb') as video and caption=description; else call existing sendPhoto. Single if/else block, no other changes.
advanced_version: Add file size validation, MIME type detection, async upload with progress tracking, retry logic for network failures, and structured logging of video send success/failure metrics — all while maintaining the same fallback contract.
